title: Counting Microalgae Culture Density
author: Jakub Nedbal
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bd8ni9ve
materials: Mark down the temperature on the shaker. Thermometer on the illuminated orbital shaker platform.

steps.title: Sterilize workspace and prepare tools
steps.instruction: Wipe down the sterile laminar flow cabinet with 70 % denatured ethanol solution. Inside the cabinet, set out a clean hemocytometer, a P20 pipette, and pipette tips.

steps.title: Dissociate cell clumps by vortexing
steps.instruction: Vortex D. quadricauda culture for at least 5 seconds and C. vulgaris culture for at least 30 seconds, vortexing thoroughly but not so vigorously that the cotton‑wool plug splashes; avoid soaking the plug with the suspension.

steps.title: Break stubborn C. vulgaris clumps
steps.instruction: If C. vulgaris cells have formed clumps on flask walls, aseptically draw the culture into a 20 mL syringe fitted with a 21 G needle, then expel back into the flask, directing the jet at the wall; repeat draw/expel ≈10 times to disperse clumps.

steps.title: Transfer flask and handle cotton plug
steps.instruction: Place a clean hemocytometer with its coverslip into the laminar flow hood. Bring the culture flask into the hood, remove its aluminium foil, spray the tweezers with 70 % denatured ethanol and let dry. Using sterilized tweezers, lift the cotton‑wool plug, keep it held, remove it from the flask opening, and keep it until it can be re‑plugged.

steps.title: Load first hemocytometer chamber
steps.instruction: Pipette 10 µL of the algal culture with the P20 pipette and load it into one chamber of the hemocytometer.

steps.title: Resuspend cells and load second chamber
steps.instruction: Shake the flask to resuspend any settled cells, then pipette another 10 µL sample using a fresh tip and load the second chamber of the hemocytometer.

steps.title: Reseal flask and return to shaker
steps.instruction: Replace the cotton‑wool plug and aluminium‑foil cap on the flask, reseal it, and return the flask to the orbital shaker.

steps.title: Place hemocytometer on microscope
steps.instruction: Carry the loaded hemocytometer to a microscope equipped with a 10× phase‑contrast objective and sufficient working distance; position it on the stage for counting.

steps.title: Count Desmodesmus quadricauda coenobia
steps.instruction: Using the Hemocytometer Sidekick app, count coenobia (not individual cells) in both chambers, focusing on the eight outer squares of each chamber. Perform three separate counts: coenobia containing two cells, four cells, and eight cells. For non‑canonical coenobia, apply the approximation rule (e.g., two singlets = one doublet; two triplets = one quadruple + one double; a triplet + singlet = one quadruple).

steps.title: Calculate D. quadricauda cell density
steps.instruction: Multiply the count of 2‑cell coenobia by 2, 4‑cell coenobia by 4, and 8‑cell coenobia by 8; sum these values to obtain total cells per square. Average the total cells over the 20 squares and multiply by 10 000 mL⁻¹ to get cells · mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Clean hemocytometer and load C. vulgaris
steps.instruction: Clean the hemocytometer and coverslip with 70 % denatured alcohol using Kimwipes (or equivalent). Load C. vulgaris sample into the hemocytometer as described in steps 5–6.

steps.title: Count Chlorella vulgaris cells
steps.instruction: With the Hemocytometer Sidekick app, count cells in both chambers but only in the four squares forming a plus sign. If culture density exceeds 5 × 10⁶ mL⁻¹, count a subset of sub‑rectangles in each square and later scale the count.

steps.title: Calculate C. vulgaris cell density
steps.instruction: When only four of the 20 sub‑rectangles are counted, multiply the obtained number by 5 to estimate cells per square (or set a dilution factor of 8 in the app). Average the cells over the eight squares and multiply by 10 000 mL⁻¹ to obtain cells · mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Final cleaning and shutdown
steps.instruction: Clean the hemocytometer and coverslip again with 70 % denatured alcohol using Kimwipes. Clean the sterile flow hood, tidy the workspace, and turn off the microscope lamp.
